subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The Love and relationships cluster poems
Themes and meanings across the cluster
Poets' methods: language, form and structure

questions.q: Which poet wrote 'Bright Star', one of the poems in the OCR Love and relationships cluster?
questions.explain: 'Bright Star' is a sonnet by the Romantic poet John Keats.

questions.q: 'Warming Her Pearls' in the cluster was written by which poet?
questions.explain: Carol Ann Duffy wrote 'Warming Her Pearls', a dramatic monologue voiced by a maid.

questions.q: Which cluster poem, about rediscovering the self after a relationship, was written by Derek Walcott?
questions.explain: 'Love After Love' is Derek Walcott's poem about learning to welcome and love yourself again.

questions.q: 'In Paris With You' is a poem in the cluster written by whom?
questions.explain: 'In Paris With You' is by James Fenton, spoken by a wary lover on the rebound.

questions.q: 'Love and Friendship', which likens love to a rose-briar and friendship to a holly-tree, is by which poet?
questions.explain: Emily Bronte wrote 'Love and Friendship', contrasting fleeting love with enduring friendship.

questions.q: Which of these contemporary poets features in the current OCR Love and relationships cluster?
questions.explain: Raymond Antrobus is among the newer, diverse voices added to the OCR Love and relationships cluster.

questions.q: 'Dusting the Phone', about anxiously waiting for a lover to call, was written by which poet?
questions.explain: Jackie Kay wrote 'Dusting the Phone', capturing the restless waiting of love.

questions.q: 'A Song' in the cluster was written by which eighteenth-century poet?
questions.explain: 'A Song' is by Helen Maria Williams, the earliest poet represented in the cluster.

questions.q: 'Love After Love' by Derek Walcott is chiefly concerned with which idea?
options: Learning to love and welcome yourself again after a relationship ends
Falling in love at first sight
Grief over the death of a parent
questions.explain: The poem urges the reader to greet themselves 'arriving at your own door', celebrating self-reconciliation.

questions.q: How is the speaker's attitude to romance best described in 'In Paris With You'?
options: Wary and anti-romantic, still wounded from a previous relationship
questions.explain: The speaker is 'on the rebound' and resists conventional romantic clichés throughout the poem.

questions.q: What does 'I Wouldn't Thank You for a Valentine' by Liz Lochhead primarily do?
options: Rejects clichéd, commercialised expressions of romance
questions.explain: Lochhead's speaker mocks the sentimental, commercial trappings of Valentine's Day.

questions.q: 'Warming Her Pearls' is written as a dramatic monologue in the voice of which figure?
options: A maid who secretly desires her mistress
questions.explain: The maid warms her mistress's pearls against her own skin, expressing unspoken longing.

questions.q: 'Morning Song' opens, 'Love set you going like a fat gold watch.' This simile mainly conveys which effect?
options: The baby as a newly-started life, described with a note of detachment
A father's pride in his family
questions.explain: The mechanical image presents the newborn as a set-going object, hinting at Plath's ambivalence.

questions.q: Robert Browning's 'Now' seeks to capture which experience of love?
options: The intensity of a single, fleeting moment
A mother's love for her child
Grief at the loss of a friend
questions.explain: 'Now' concentrates on one supreme, momentary union rather than lasting devotion.

questions.q: In which poetic form is Keats's 'Bright Star' written?
questions.explain: 'Bright Star' is a fourteen-line sonnet expressing a wish for steadfast, constant love.

questions.q: Sylvia Plath's 'Morning Song' is centrally about which subject?
options: A mother's complex feelings towards her newborn baby
questions.explain: The poem explores tender yet uneasy maternal feelings in the hours after birth.

questions.q: A student wants to compare how two poems present the anxieties and insecurities of love. Which pairing is most suitable?
options: 'In Paris With You' and 'Dusting the Phone'
questions.explain: Both poems foreground uncertainty and unease, making them a strong comparison of love's anxieties.

questions.q: A student notes a poem uses a first-person speaker who is not the poet, revealing character while addressing another figure. Which term best describes this method?
questions.explain: A dramatic monologue is voiced by a distinct persona, as in 'Warming Her Pearls'.

questions.q: In the OCR comparative question, the strongest analysis of 'methods' would concentrate on which of the following?
options: How each poet's use of form, structure and language shapes meaning
How many lines each poem contains
The poets' birth and death dates
A plot summary of each poem
questions.explain: OCR rewards comparison of poets' methods and their effects, not mere content summary or facts.

questions.q: A student wants to pair a poem exploring the recovery of one's own identity after heartbreak. Which named cluster poem fits best as a partner?
questions.explain: 'Love After Love' centres on reclaiming the self after love, making it ideal for that theme.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) English Literature (J352) specification; Love & Relationships Anthology
